entities.summary:
Bérenger de Landore (1262–1330) was a French Dominican and prominent figure in the Order of Preachers, who played a crucial role in the medieval religious landscape. He rose through the ranks to become Master of the Order (1312–1317) and later Archbishop of Santiago de Compostela (1317–1330).


De Landore's tenure as Archbishop was marked by his efforts to reform the church and promote the interests of the Dominican Order. He also engaged in diplomatic efforts to maintain the fragile peace between the Catholic Church and the secular powers of his time.


Bérenger de Landore's legacy is complex and multifaceted, reflecting both the grandeur and fragility of medieval Catholicism. His story serves as a reminder of the intricate web of power, influence, and faith that shaped the course of human history.
